completeness.why: getNextDate and getUpcomingDates pass their own skip flag and mode to applyWeekendRule, which now decides whether and how to move the date (getNextDate keeps only its site-specific noSkipWeekend guard); both schedule-template sites call applyWeekendRule but keep their own outer dateConditions.value.skipWeekend ? ... : nextBaseDate ternary, so whether the rule applies is still decided there as well.

interface.why: applyWeekendRule(date, {skipWeekend, weekendSolveMode}) takes exactly the real variation, each caller maps its own field name (weekendSolve vs weekendSolveMode) explicitly, and noSkipWeekend stays at its one site; the rule object accepts whole condition objects loosely typed, a minor weakness.

disguised_duplication.where: The old helper is replaced rather than kept beside a copy; the schedule-template sites keep a redundant skipWeekend check, which is visible rather than disguised.
